text:
Ava: Hey team, new hire here. Need kube access for dev+staging and namespace 'avadev'. Also want to port-forward a pod and make sure I don’t accidentally get prod in my kubeconfig. Quick advice?

Sam (DevEx): Welcome! :wave: Short flow: submit access form for namespace + kubeconfig, SRE approves, they mint a scoped kubeconfig (dev/staging only). We include a merge helper so prod stays out of your local config.

Ravi (eng-infra): Implementation detail: we create a serviceaccount in 'avadev' and issue a kubeconfig tied to that SA via short-lived tokens. By default tokens rotate every 24h; onboarding requests commonly get 30d.

Nina (SRE): For port-forwarding we grant pods/portforward in the namespace Role. kubectl proxy is allowed too for UI debugging. If your manager is OOO, add the alternate approver on the form and we hit the on-call alias.

Ava: Thanks! Any merge snippet to avoid touching prod?

Sam (DevEx): Use this: `export KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/config:./ava-kc.yaml && kubectl config view --merge --flatten >/tmp/k && mv /tmp/k ~/.kube/config && kubectl config use-context redwood-dev/ava`. We also attach a one-liner in the ticket.

access-bot: Access request created AR-4902 — namespace: avadev, clusters: dev,staging, duration: 30d. https://redwood.internal/requests/AR-4902

Nina (SRE): Approved (fallback manager confirmed). Kubeconfig attached to ticket; check and run the merge snippet.

Ava: Confirmed merged and `kubectl get pods -n avadev` returns our pods. Port-forward worked. Appreciate the help!
